I am an old woman of 76 years, and I have been farming cassava and cocoyam on this small rented land here in the South South for many seasons. I have no money for chemical fertilizer — the price is too high, and the seller is far. I will plant the cassava stems I saved from last year's harvest, like my mother taught me, and I will put the household waste and some goat droppings around the plants. My son and his wife will help me with the clearing and planting, but my back is not strong like before, so I may call one or two young men from the village to help with the heavy clearing.
